speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your dizziness and vertigo, could you please describe exactly what these episodes feel like and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Do you experience any ringing in your ears (tinnitus) or a feeling of fullness in the ear during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the dizziness is position-dependent, so does moving your head to a specific position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up, consistently trigger the spinning sensation? Also, do you have any nausea or vomiting associated with these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No history of Meniere's disease, vestibular neuritis, or labyrinthitis. Social history: Retired school teacher. Lives alone. Non-smoker, occasional wine. Enjoys light gardening.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have no significant past medical history. To help narrow this down, does the dizziness start immediately when you change position, or is there a short delay before the spinning sensation begins? Also, do you experience any double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your arms or legs?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headache, tinnitus, hearing loss, nausea, vomiting, or recent respiratory infections.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you, those negative findings help rule out several other causes. I would like to perform a physical exam to confirm the source of your vertigo; please lie back with your head turned 45 degrees to the right while I gently lift your head into extension and observe for nystagmus.

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver
